title: A minor's chat and wellbeing data leaks through a contractor export

text: Monitoring alert: a debugging export of chat logs (412 student records, Grades 9-11, ages 14-17: names, class, planner entries and wellbeing check-in notes) was written to a publicly readable storage bucket by a contractor's script on Sunday night. Access logs show three downloads from unknown IP addresses.

rationale: The breach affects personal data of minors in grades 9-11. Under PDPL Article (9) and (10), the Controller must notify the Data Protection Bureau and affected data subjects if the breach prejudices privacy confidentiality. Under Child Digital Safety Law Article (7), parental consent mechanisms and data minimization apply to children under 13, but these students are 14-17, so the breach triggers notification duties. The Processor (schools) must be alerted per PDPL Article (10)(3). A Data Protection Officer may be required per PDPL Article (11) if high risk or large volume of sensitive data is involved. Immediate containment and notification are needed.

actions.action: Notify the Data Protection Bureau and affected students/guardians per PDPL Articles (9) and (10), citing the breach and remedial steps taken.
Alert the school processor(s) and request they notify their Data Protection Officers, per PDPL Article (10)(3).
Verify whether a Data Protection Officer is designated for Murshid/platform; if not, initiate designation per PDPL Article (11).
Conduct forensic review of the storage bucket; ensure public access is revoked and the contractor's script is audited.
Report the incident to the Child Digital Safety Council if minors' data exposure meets thresholds under Federal Decree-Law No. 26 of 2025.

text: A parent emails the school counsellor: her son's Murshid wellbeing note about exam stress has been posted in a student WhatsApp group. The school did not know Murshid stored wellbeing notes.

rationale: The incident involves sensitive student wellbeing data being shared without authorization in a public forum (WhatsApp group). KB #khda-distance-learning-2026#0019 requires schools to stay vigilant for signs of student stress and maintain active safeguarding responsibilities. KB #khda-distance-learning-2026#0021 obliges schools to treat students receiving abusive messages outside lesson time as active wellbeing and safeguarding concerns, document actions, and communicate with families. The school must address both the privacy breach and the safeguarding implications of exam stress being exposed.

actions.action: Immediately suspend Murshid's access to wellbeing note storage and review all recent data exports to identify the scope of the breach and how the WhatsApp group post occurred.

Direct the School Data Protection Officers to conduct a full access audit of Murshid's systems, revoke unnecessary permissions, and implement stricter data classification controls for sensitive wellbeing notes.
Prepare and send formal communication to the affected parent and guardian community explaining the breach, the steps being taken, and reassurance about future data protection measures.

Within 48 hours: Complete access audit and implement corrective controls  [UNSUPPORTED: '48' not in any cited source]

rationale: Article (9) of the PDPL mandates that the Controller notify the Data Subject when a breach would prejudice privacy/confidentiality, and notify the Bureau per Clause (1). Article (10) requires the Controller/Processor to designate a Data Protection Officer in specific high-risk cases (e.g., new technologies, large volume of Sensitive Personal Data, systematic assessment). The operator must fulfill both obligations: notify the Bureau and affected data subjects, and confirm or designate a DPO.

Verify or designate a Data Protection Officer per Article (10), ensuring the officer has sufficient skills/knowledge of personal data protection law and notifying the Bureau of their contact details.

deadlines: Breach notification to Bureau and data subjects without undue delay and within the period set by Executive Regulations; DPO designation prior to or concurrent with processing activities involving high-risk data.

rationale: The MOE must respond to the incident to ensure compliance with the National AI Literacy Curriculum Framework, UAE AI Ethics Guidelines (2022), and the National AI Strategy 2031. The framework emphasizes students understanding AI as designed technologies, data-driven decision-making, and critical analysis of system design. Ethics guidelines require informing users of AI interaction extent and significant AI-assisted decisions. The MOE needs to clarify expectations for platform compliance, particularly regarding student data, transparency, and age-appropriate design.

actions.action: Request detailed incident report from Murshid operator including student age group, nature of interaction, and any data collection or decision-making aspects.

Issue guidance to private schools on the MoE curriculum regarding acceptable AI tutor platform features for different age groups, referencing the National AI Literacy Curriculum Framework K-12 age-appropriate strands and UAE AI Ethics transparency requirements.
Coordinate with KHDA to assess whether the platform meets existing MoE-approved tools list criteria, or if a temporary suspension is needed pending review.

text: A guardian files a complaint with the UAE Data Office saying an AI study app leaked her daughter's personal data and nobody has told her what happened.
Forensics update: the bucket belongs to the model-logging vendor and is hosted outside the UAE. 37 of the 412 records came in through a school-connector licence; the rest are family accounts.

rationale: The complaint triggers breach notification obligations under PDPL Articles 9-10 (notification to data subject and Bureau). The MoE request requires assessment of Murshid's data collection and compliance. I must verify what data Murshid collected, whether breach notifications were properly issued, and if security measures per Article 20 were adequate. The guardian's lack of notification suggests possible non-compliance with the duty to inform data subjects of breaches prejudicing privacy (Article 9.2).

actions.action: Request Murshid operator to disclose what personal data of students was collected, the legal basis for processing, and whether a breach notification was sent to affected data subjects and the Bureau under PDPL Articles 9-10.

Assess Murshid's security measures against Article 20 requirements, evaluating data processing risks, nature/scope/purposes of processing, and whether appropriate technical/pseudonymisation measures were implemented.
Check whether an Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) was conducted under Article 21, given Murshid's status as an AI education processor handling student data.
Verify if Murshid complied with MoE student data privacy guidelines and UAE AI Ethics Principle 8 (privacy preservation) per uae-ai-ethics-guidelines-2022#0032.

The school must balance support with compliance to age verification and data protection rules under Federal Decree-Law No. 26 of 2025.
